title: Baby Books & Lap Rhymes
strapline: A book on a lap and a rhyme with a bounce — where a lifelong love of stories begins.
intent: Babies experience books as warm, joyful and shared — the foundation of a lifelong love of reading.
Babies hear the rhythm, melody and repeated sounds of rhymes, tuning their ears to language.
Babies build early vocabulary as an adult names the pictures they point to and gaze at.
Babies learn how books work — turning pages, pointing, that pictures mean something.
Babies deepen their bond with a key adult through the closeness of lap-time and song.
implementation: Keep sturdy board books, cloth books and flap books within babies' reach in a cosy, comfortable corner.
Follow the baby's lead — let them turn pages, chew the corner, go back to a favourite spread, skip ahead.
Name what the baby points to and looks at: 'that's a dog — woof woof!' and pause for their response.
Sing lap rhymes with bounces, tickles and actions — 'Row Row', 'Round and Round the Garden', 'This Little Piggy'.
Repeat the same books and rhymes often — the repetition is exactly what babies need and love.
Read one-to-one and in tiny groups, keeping it snuggly and unhurried.
Use lots of expression, sound effects and pauses so the sharing is lively and responsive.
key_questions: Where's the doggy — can you point?
Round and round the garden... what comes next?
What can you see on this page?
Do you want this one again?

impact.text: Babies enjoy sharing books and show favourites.
Babies join in with rhymes through movement, sound and delight.
Babies point to and look at pictures as an adult names them.
Babies handle books, turning pages and exploring how they work.
Babies bond closely through shared lap-time and song.

enhancements: A basket of touch-and-feel and flap books to explore with hands.
A rhyme-time bag with props — a duck for 'Five Little Ducks', a spider for 'Incy Wincy'.
Family photo books so babies see faces they love.
Mirror books and high-contrast books for the youngest babies.
A cosy den or cushioned nook for one-to-one sharing.
Songs and rhymes played softly to hum along to through the day.

playing_exploring: Babies explore books freely — turning, patting, mouthing, pointing.
They choose which book to bring and which page to linger on.
active_learning: Babies return to a favourite book or rhyme over and over.
creating_thinking: Babies anticipate the tickle or the next line, joining in on cue.
